    Doing,
    Review,
    Done,
    Blocked,

    L,

    pub title: String,

    #[serde(default)]

    999

cards.title: Five stores and atomic storage
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Five persistent stores: identity.md, user.md, memory/, journal/, loops.md.
  • Plain Markdown; directories 0700, files 0600; write to a temporary file, then rename.
  • Memory split into preferences.md / lessons.md; one journal file per month, merged by day.
  • Civil dates computed in-tree, no timezone dependency.

Acceptance

  • Round-trip tests for all five stores.
  • Same-day journal appends merge; different days stay ordered.
  • Permissions verified as 0700 / 0600.
  • Missing identity.md returns None instead of a fabricated empty string.

Notes

Markdown is the only format: for a single user under 200 entries, files are the best query engine. Saving rewrites the layout, so hand-written comments may disappear; that is the accepted cost.

cards.title: Prompt assembly and in-band protocol
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Stable prefix: persona → identity → user → memory → protocol.
  • Volatile sections last: today → loops → journal.
  • Section budgets: 600 each for identity and user, 2000 for memory, 300 for loops, 600 for journal.
  • In-band protocol: <<niuse:memory>>, <<niuse:loop>>, <<niuse:journal>>.
  • Streaming strip needs a tail buffer; unterminated blocks stay visible.

Acceptance

  • Section order covered by a test; expired memory excluded; entries older than 30 days marked unverified.
  • Oversized identity is truncated and labelled.
  • Protocol tests cover blocks split across chunks, partial prefixes, false markers, and unterminated blocks.
  • In real calls the candidate block is stripped and the prose is intact.

Notes

The original plan had memory and loop blocks only. To avoid a second model call, a journal block was added and is written automatically.

cards.title: REPL and the niucode driver
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Interactive REPL: streaming output, slash commands, Ctrl-C cancel, Ctrl-D exit.
  • The driver opens or resumes thread.jsonl and rebuilds history with project_history.
  • Each turn sets the working directory again, proving per-turn cwd on one session.
  • Candidate confirmation: y / n / e / s; conflicts use r / k / d.

Acceptance

  • A real provider run completes a read-only task and persists the session.
  • The same session reads in one directory, /cd /tmp, then reads in another; both succeed.
  • Confirming a candidate writes memory that niuse mem list can show.
  • Journal and loop blocks are written automatically.
  • The driver is about 200 lines and does not bypass the loop.

Notes

At MVP time niucode-cli was a binary with no library target, so its TUI and renderer could not be reused. ADR-0032 has since added the library target and TurnHooks; the MVP still ships a minimal renderer until those hooks are wired and the front end moves.

cards.title: Soft expiry, conflicts, secret scan
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Normal injection within 30 days; unverified from 31 to 90; not injected after 90.
  • Conflict detection via character-bigram Jaccard: ≥ 0.5 is similar; same tag lowers the bar to 0.35.
  • Secret patterns: sk-, ghp_, github_pat_, AKIA, private-key blocks, Slack, Google, long hex.
  • Refusal is the default; the CLI needs --force to override.

Acceptance

  • Common key shapes match; ordinary Chinese prose and short hex do not.
  • Tests for similar, unrelated, and same-tag pairs.
  • A real sk-... input is refused with exit code 1.
  • Expired memory is excluded from the prompt.

Notes

Scanning is a backstop, not a guarantee. Private projects, client names, and internal addresses still rely on human judgement at confirmation time.

cards.title: Cold start and the review queue
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap [--limit N] [--since-days N] scans ~/.niucode/sessions.
  • Only user / assistant text is sent; tool output is dropped.
  • One tool-free extraction returns {kind, text, tags} and writes inbox.md.
  • niuse review walks the queue with y / n / s / q; accepted entries become memory.

Acceptance

  • Empty sessions are skipped; only sessions with dialogue cost a model call.
  • Candidates are deduplicated against existing memory and within the batch.
  • Inbox format has a round-trip test.
  • A real run mined a sandbox lesson that review accepted into memory.

Notes

Default cap is 40 sessions. Cost is roughly 2k input tokens per session, one-off.

cards.title: Architecture dashboard
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Reuse niucode's xtask generator and three-column shell, with a niuse project model.
  • Four views: Architecture (default), Work, Docs, Decisions.
  • Sources: project.json plus board/*.md plus docs/**/*.md.
  • Single-file docs/index.html, offline, no CDN, no runtime fetch.
  • cargo xtask dashboard --check fails when generated output is stale.

Acceptance

  • cargo xtask dashboard writes docs/index.html and model.json.
  • Validation passes: module paths exist, card references resolve, ADR statuses are legal.
  • Architecture shows modules, layers, and dependency arrows.
  • Docs opens the architecture doc, the plan, and both ADRs.
  • --check passes.

Notes

The board is read-only; state changes go through the repository so it never becomes a second source of truth. The generator is copied from niucode; only branding and the project model changed.

cards.title: Ten working days of dogfood
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • At least one real task per day goes through niuse, not niucode.
  • Record proposals, acceptances, and concrete cases where memory saved a round of explanation.
  • At least once it should disagree and change your mind.
  • Keep the store under 50 entries; more means the bar is too low.

Acceptance

  • Ten consecutive working days.
  • Candidate acceptance rate ≥ 60%.
  • At least 3 correct citations of a past judgement.
  • At least 1 case of being persuaded.
  • At least 1 A/B case where NIUSE_MEMORY=off changes the answer.

Notes

Record one row per day in the dogfood log. This card writes no code. Its job is to stop new features before the current ones are validated.

cards.title: Show a full unified diff at approval
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Render ChangePreview as unified hunks: file header, @@ ranges, context, additions, removals.
  • Reuse niucode's Toolbox::preview result; niuse copies no path policy and performs no extra reads.
  • Cap the rendered diff at 80 lines with an explicit "more line(s)" marker.
  • Keep the approval prompt below the diff; non-TTY still falls back to a line reply.

Acceptance

  • Write / edit approval shows real hunks with + and - lines.
  • A new file is marked as new; command and note previews still render.
  • Long previews are capped instead of flooding the terminal.
  • Rendering has unit tests; the security boundary is unchanged.

Notes

This was the last known gap between niuse's approval prompt and niucode's TUI preview.

cards.title: Memory recall across expired entries
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem search <query> [--fresh] searches every saved memory, including expired ones.
  • /mem recall <query> does the same inside the REPL.
  • Ranking prefers substring and tag matches over character-bigram similarity, which is weak for short queries.
  • Results show age, expiry state, tags, and the entry id.

Acceptance

  • Expired entries are searchable but still excluded from injection.
  • --fresh hides expired entries.
  • Substring and tag matches outrank unrelated entries; threshold is 0.2.
  • Core scoring has unit tests; CLI and REPL paths were exercised manually.

Notes

Recall is the reason expired memory is kept instead of deleted: it leaves the prompt, not the store.

cards.title: Acceptance metrics and stats
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • ~/.niuse/metrics.jsonl: tab-separated local counters, file 0600.
  • Record turn outcomes, candidate proposals and decisions, journal writes, loops, manual memories, and bootstrap review decisions.
  • niuse stats [--days N] and /stats summarise the window; --days 0 means all time.
  • Acceptance rate is accepted over proposed; edited and replace/keep decisions count as accepted.

Acceptance

  • Metrics append atomically and stay 0600.
  • Parsing and summarisation have unit tests, including a window filter.
  • The CLI and REPL expose the summary.
  • No memory text is written to the metrics file.

Notes

exec turns are counted in the same turn series. Candidates printed by exec are not counted as proposals, because no decision is collected.

This is the measurement M2-001 needs: without it, "acceptance rate ≥ 60%" is a feeling. The file is local-only and excluded from injection.

cards.title: Doctor health check
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse doctor and /doctor check the home directory and mode, identity, user profile, memory counts, thread readability, metrics, credentials, bwrap, and the niucode pin.
  • Offline: no model call, no network.
  • Failures return a non-zero exit; warnings do not.
  • The pin check only runs inside a checkout where niucode.rev exists.

Acceptance

  • A healthy store reports zero failures.
  • Missing credentials are a failure; missing identity or bwrap is a warning.
  • A drifted sibling checkout is reported with the sync command.
  • Report counters have a unit test.

Notes

Doctor is the onboarding answer to "why will it not run": one command, explicit levels, and the exact next step.

cards.title: Manual loops
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse loops add <text> [--due YYYY-MM-DD] creates a promise without waiting for the model to emit a block.
  • /loop <text> does the same inside the REPL.
  • Due dates are validated; invalid dates are rejected before anything is written.
  • Secret scanning applies to manual loops too.
  • Creation is recorded in metrics.

Acceptance

  • A manual loop persists with an optional due date.
  • An invalid due date writes nothing and exits non-zero.
  • The REPL path records the loop and a metric.
  • The CLI listing shows open and overdue entries.

Notes

The model is not the only source of promises. This closes the gap where you know something needs tracking but the turn did not produce a loop block.

cards.title: Memory maintenance: show and edit
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem show <id> prints kind, tags, created, confirmed, source, and text.
  • niuse mem edit <id> opens the text in $EDITOR, normalises it to one line, rescans for secrets, and refreshes the confirmation date.
  • /mem show <id> works in the REPL; candidate editing reuses the same editor helper.
  • IDs accept m-, l-, or no prefix.

Acceptance

  • Show prints every field a reviewer needs.
  • Edit updates the text and confirmed date, or reports no change.
  • A secret in the edited text is refused and the stored entry is untouched.
  • The editor helper is shared with candidate editing; ID prefixes have a test.

Notes

Correcting a wrong memory is as important as adding one: a bad entry is injected on every turn until it is fixed.

cards.title: Journal search
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse journal --search <query> ranks journal bullets across all months.
  • /journal search <query> does the same in the REPL.
  • Ranking reuses the memory scorer: substring hits first, bigram similarity above 0.2.
  • Results show the date and the bullet, capped at ten.

Acceptance

  • A substring hit is found and keeps its date.
  • An unrelated query returns no rows.
  • The CLI and REPL paths were exercised.
  • Ranking and empty-result behaviour have unit tests.

Notes

Memory answers "what is true"; the journal answers "when did we decide this". Search is what makes the second question cheap.

cards.title: Markdown export
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse export [--out FILE] [--session PATH] projects a session log to Markdown.
  • User and assistant turns keep their order; tool calls and results are fenced.
  • Protocol blocks are stripped, exactly as the REPL strips them.
  • Tool output is clipped at 4,000 characters; exported files are 0600.

Acceptance

  • Turns render in order with a metadata header.
  • Protocol blocks never leak into the export.
  • Long tool output is clipped with a marker.
  • Writes to --out are private; stdout works without a file.
  • Unit tests cover ordering, clipping, and block stripping.

Notes

The event log remains the source of truth. The export is a read-only projection for review, backup, or attaching a transcript to an issue.

cards.title: Config file defaults
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • ~/.niuse/config.toml with a [defaults] table: provider, model, sandbox, approval, network, max_steps.
  • Precedence is CLI flag → config file → built-in default.
  • niuse config init writes a commented template; config show prints the file.
  • Settings resolve lazily: offline commands (mem, loops, journal, export, status, stats) do not read the config, so a broken file cannot block them.
  • Config files are 0600.

Acceptance

  • TOML parsing and the precedence rule have unit tests.
  • A config sandbox changes the REPL banner; a CLI flag overrides it.
  • A malformed config fails agent commands with the file path, but status still works.
  • Init refuses to overwrite without --force.

Notes

Defaults belong in a file, not in muscle memory. Lazy resolution is deliberate: a typo in config.toml should not make niuse mem show unusable.

cards.title: Manual journal entries and identity editing
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse journal --add <text> and /journal add <text> append a bullet to today.
  • niuse identity show|edit and /identity edit open the identity file in $EDITOR.
  • Journal entries are secret-scanned and recorded in metrics.
  • Editing uses a multiline helper; memory and candidate editing keep the one-line normaliser.

Acceptance

  • A manual journal entry appears in recent_journal and in search.
  • Identity editing writes the file and keeps it 0600.
  • Empty edits report "no change" and do not write.
  • The journal path has a unit test; identity editing was exercised with a scripted editor.

Notes

Not every durable line comes from the model. Manual entry is the escape hatch when a block was not emitted.

cards.title: Bootstrap inbox merge
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Re-running niuse bootstrap merges into the existing queue instead of replacing it.
  • Pending entries that have since been accepted into memory are dropped.
  • Secret-bearing entries are dropped from both sides.
  • New candidates are deduplicated against memory, the existing queue, and each other.

Acceptance

  • Pending entries survive a second run; accepted ones disappear.
  • Duplicate candidates are not queued twice.
  • The merge rule has a unit test.
  • The CLI reports new versus total pending.

Notes

Cold start is not a one-shot operation: sessions accumulate, and a second mining pass should add to the queue, not erase it.

cards.title: Thread rotation
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • /new appends a session end, archives the current thread to ~/.niuse/threads/thread-<millis>.jsonl, and opens a fresh default thread.
  • --thread PATH resumes an archived thread without changing the default.
  • The archive keeps the original JSONL untouched; history comes from the normal projection.
  • /status reports the active thread, not the default path.

Acceptance

  • /new archives the old file and creates a fresh three-event session.
  • --thread resumes an archive and reports its event count.
  • A missing archive source is a no-op.
  • Archive moves have unit tests.

Notes

The default remains one continuous relationship. /new is a chapter break, not the normal path; old chapters stay readable and resumable.

cards.title: Piped output exits cleanly
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse ... | head no longer panics when the reader closes early; the process exits 0.
  • Only the "Broken pipe" panic is intercepted; every other panic goes to the default hook unchanged.
  • The fix is a panic hook rather than a global SIGPIPE reset, because SIGPIPE also covers socket writes made by the provider.

Acceptance

  • niuse mem list | head -1 exits 0 with no panic output.
  • niuse status | head -1 behaves the same.
  • Non-pipe panics still print through the default hook.
  • niuse status --thread <archive> reports the requested thread.

Notes

Small, but it was the first papercut hit while testing; a CLI that panics when paged is not pleasant to script against.

cards.title: Thread listing
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse threads lists the active thread and every archive under ~/.niuse/threads/.
  • Each row shows age, event count, size, and the path relative to the niuse home.
  • The active thread is marked with *, respecting --thread.
  • Invalid sessions still appear with an event count of zero rather than hiding.

Acceptance

  • The active thread and one archive are both listed.
  • The active marker follows --thread / the default path.
  • Age and size formatting have unit tests.
  • Listing is read-only and does not open sessions for append.

Notes

/new made archives; without a listing they were only discoverable with ls. This closes the loop.

cards.title: Expired memory pruning
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem prune lists entries older than 90 days and changes nothing.
  • niuse mem prune --apply removes exactly those entries and records a metric.
  • Fresh and stale-but-valid entries are untouched.
  • Deletion is explicit; there is no implicit expiry write path.

Acceptance

  • Dry run lists the expired entry and leaves the store unchanged.
  • --apply removes only expired entries; a fresh lesson survives.
  • The removal path has a unit test.
  • The metric records how many entries were pruned.

Notes

Soft expiry means expired entries already leave the prompt. Pruning is housekeeping for the file, not a behaviour change; that is why it is manual.

cards.title: Stats daily trend
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse stats --trend adds a per-day breakdown for the selected window; the window is N local calendar days, not a rolling 24-hour clock.
  • Days are local calendar dates; each row shows turns, accepted/proposed, and acceptance.
  • At most the last fourteen active days are printed.
  • /stats keeps the summary view; the flag is CLI-only for now.

Acceptance

  • Metrics on two local days produce two rows.
  • Acceptance is - on days without proposals.
  • Grouping has a unit test with synthetic timestamps.
  • A real metrics file renders without panics.

Notes

The dogfood question is not "what is the total" but "is it getting better"; a daily view makes that visible.

cards.title: Bootstrap dry run
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap --dry-run selects sessions exactly as a real run would, then stops.
  • It prints each session id and the transcript size in characters.
  • No provider request is made, so the preview is free.
  • Empty or tool-only sessions are still filtered before the preview.

Acceptance

  • Dry run lists the selected sessions and their transcript sizes.
  • No model call and no inbox write.
  • The selection path is shared with the real run.
  • The CLI path was exercised with a real session directory.

Notes

Bootstrap can cost a model call per session; a free preview is the difference between "try it" and "avoid it".

cards.title: Manual memory duplicate guard
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem add runs the same similarity rule as candidate writes.
  • A match prints the similar ids and refuses unless --force is passed.
  • --force now overrides both the secret scan and the duplicate check; the help text says so.
  • Candidate and manual writes therefore share one conflict definition.

Acceptance

  • A near-duplicate manual add is refused and lists the existing id.
  • --force adds it and the store grows to two entries.
  • The guard has a unit test.
  • Secret scanning still runs before the duplicate check.

Notes

The confirmation flow already prevented duplicates; the manual path was the hole. Closing it keeps the store reviewable at 50 entries.

cards.title: Dogfood record tooling
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse stats --json emits a stable summary plus per-day rows for scripting.
  • docs/dogfood.md defines the ten-day ritual: one row per day, two numbers, one sentence.
  • The JSON includes turns, candidate decisions, acceptance, activity counts, and days.
  • /stats keeps the human summary; --json is CLI-only.

Acceptance

  • JSON output parses and includes acceptance_percent and days.
  • Serialization has a unit test with synthetic metrics.
  • The dogfood guide links the exact command and a table template.
  • README points at the guide.

Notes

The point of the JSON is not dashboards; it is making the daily row cheap enough to actually write.

cards.title: User profile editing
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse user show|edit and /user / /user edit expose user.md.
  • Editing uses the multiline $EDITOR helper and keeps the file 0600.
  • A missing file opens a small template with the three questions that matter: current work, working style, red lines.
  • The edit is recorded in metrics.

Acceptance

  • Show prints the path and content, or a hint when missing.
  • Edit writes the file through a scripted editor and user show reflects it.
  • Empty edits report no change.
  • Permissions remain 0600.

Notes

identity.md says who it is; user.md says who you are. The second one had no manual path, only bootstrap.

cards.title: Bootstrap profile draft
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap --profile makes one extra model call and drafts user.md from the selected sessions.
  • It only writes when user.md is missing or --force-profile is passed.
  • Input is capped at 10k characters; output is asked for three sections and no speculation.
  • --dry-run reports that a profile would be drafted without calling anything.
  • The write is recorded in metrics.

Acceptance

  • A fresh home gets a user.md draft; an existing one is skipped by default.
  • The input builder respects its cap (unit test).
  • The draft is written 0600 and the command suggests niuse user edit.
  • A real run produced a draft that admitted uncertainty instead of inventing facts.

Notes

This is the missing half of the cold start described in the plan: candidates fill memory, the profile fills user.md. identity.md is still never mined.

cards.title: Secret scan for identity and profile edits
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • identity edit, user edit, and identity init scan the final text before writing.
  • bootstrap --profile refuses a generated draft that contains a secret pattern.
  • A refusal leaves the existing file untouched and exits non-zero.
  • Memory, journal, and loop writes already had the same guard.

Acceptance

  • A scripted editor inserting sk-... is refused for identity and user.
  • The existing identity file is unchanged after the refusal.
  • The profile draft path checks before write_user.
  • The scan uses the same built-in patterns as other writes.

Notes

Identity and user text is injected on every turn; a leaked key there would be sent to the provider continuously. The guard belongs at the write, not only in memory.

cards.title: Profile-only bootstrap
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse bootstrap --profile-only implies --profile and stops after drafting user.md.
  • It skips the per-session candidate extraction, saving one call per session.
  • The existing inbox is left untouched.
  • --dry-run still previews the sessions and the profile intent without a model call.

Acceptance

  • --profile-only sets the profile path even without --profile.
  • The command returns before candidate extraction.
  • Dry run reports the profile intent and lists sessions.
  • README documents the flag.

Notes

Sometimes only the "who you are" half is missing. Making the user pay for candidate extraction in that case is unnecessary.

cards.title: Machine-readable memory output
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem list --json emits the visible entries as a JSON array.
  • niuse mem search <query> --json emits ranked matches with the same shape.
  • Fields: id, kind, tags, created, confirmed, age_days, expired, source, text.
  • Expiry state is computed at read time; the file format is unchanged.

Acceptance

  • Both commands emit valid JSON that parses.
  • expired and age_days reflect the current date.
  • Serialization has a unit test.
  • Text output is unchanged when the flag is absent.

Notes

Markdown stays the storage format. JSON is an output view for scripts and dogfood, not a second store.

cards.title: Memory kind filter
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem list --kind preference|lesson filters the visible entries.
  • niuse mem search <query> --kind ... applies the same filter before ranking.
  • An unknown kind fails with the two accepted values.
  • --json respects the filter; text output keeps the global counts.

Acceptance

  • Listing lessons hides preferences.
  • Search ranks only the requested kind.
  • An invalid kind exits non-zero with a clear message.
  • Kind parsing has a unit test.

Notes

At fifty entries the list is still readable, but "show me only decisions" is a real review need.

cards.title: JSON for threads and journal
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse threads --json lists archives with a path relative to the niuse home, active flag, events, bytes, and age.
  • niuse journal --json emits day objects; with --search, hit objects with date and text.
  • The text output is unchanged when the flag is absent; --add ignores --json.
  • All three persistent stores now have a machine-readable view alongside Markdown.

Acceptance

  • Threads JSON uses relative paths and marks exactly one active thread.
  • Journal show/search JSON parse and keep dates.
  • Thread conversion has a unit test.
  • Existing text output is untouched.

Notes

Markdown remains the only storage. JSON is a read view for scripts, not a second source of truth.

cards.title: Effective config view
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse config effective prints the merged values: provider, model, sandbox, approval, network, max_steps.
  • Precedence is the same as runtime: CLI flag, then config file, then built-in.
  • max_steps = 0 is shown as unlimited; a missing model is shown as the provider default.
  • No provider or credential is constructed.
  • The doctor hint now points at bootstrap --profile and user edit.

Acceptance

  • Defaults print on a clean home.
  • CLI flags override the file in the printed view.
  • An end-to-end CLI test asserts the override.
  • The command works without network or credentials.

Notes

The raw file answers "what did I configure"; this answers "what will actually run".

cards.title: Doctor JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse doctor --json emits {checks, failures, warnings}.
  • Each check has level (ok / warn / fail), label, and detail.
  • Human output is unchanged when the flag is absent.
  • Exit semantics stay the same: failures are non-zero, warnings are zero.

Acceptance

  • JSON parses and contains every check.
  • Levels serialize in lowercase.
  • The report counters still have a unit test, now also covering serialization.
  • Existing human output is untouched.

Notes

CI and setup scripts can now assert on the same facts a human sees, instead of scraping [ok] prefixes.

cards.title: Status and loops JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse status --json emits nested memory, loops, and prompt sections plus home, thread, identity, and user flags.
  • niuse loops list --json emits id, text, due, done, and overdue.
  • Human output is unchanged when the flag is absent.
  • Both commands are covered by end-to-end CLI tests.

Acceptance

  • Status JSON parses and reports zero-state counts.
  • Loops JSON round-trips a due date.
  • Overdue is computed at read time.
  • Existing text output is untouched.

Notes

This closes the JSON surface: memory, journal, threads, loops, status, doctor, and stats all have a machine-readable view.

cards.title: Line editing and persistent history
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • The REPL uses rustyline when stdin is a terminal: cursor movement, word editing, Ctrl-A/E, and Up/Down history.
  • History persists at ~/.niuse/history, loaded at startup and saved on exit, mode 0600.
  • Piped or non-TTY stdin keeps the plain line reader, so scripts and tests are unaffected.
  • Ctrl-C at the prompt clears the line; Ctrl-D exits. During a turn, Ctrl-C still cancels as before.

Acceptance

  • A PTY session writes a private history file containing the entered lines.
  • Piped /quit still exits zero and does not create a history file.
  • History permissions are covered by a unit test.
  • Init failure falls back to the plain reader instead of aborting.

Notes

A companion you talk to every day needs arrow keys. Keeping the piped path unchanged is what lets the integration tests keep exercising the real binary.

cards.title: Per-turn usage and transcript styling
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Each turn ends with a compact usage line: input, output, and cached tokens when present.
  • Tool calls and successful tool results are dim; failures are red; warnings are yellow.
  • Styling is enabled only on a TTY and is suppressed by NO_COLOR or a pipe.
  • Token counts use 999, 1.5k, 12k; the formatter has a unit test.

Acceptance

  • A real turn printed 1.9k in · 2 out.
  • Piped output stays plain, so integration tests and exports are unaffected.
  • Formatting is covered by a unit test.
  • No new dependency for color.

Notes

Cost awareness should be one dim line, not a dashboard. The transcript remains readable when piped or when colors are disabled.

cards.title: Slash-command tab completion
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Tab at a / prefix completes against the command list, including subcommands such as /mem recall and /journal search.
  • The inserted text ends with a space, so the next keystroke starts the argument.
  • Completion is active only in the TTY editor; piped input is untouched.
  • A pure slash_candidates function is unit tested.

Acceptance

  • /mem r resolves to /mem recall.
  • Non-slash input and prefixes ending in a space return nothing.
  • Multiple matches are listed by rustyline in length order.
  • The completer adds no dependency beyond rustyline.

Notes

Twenty-odd commands are too many to memorize. Completion stays deliberately shallow: commands, not arguments or memory ids.

cards.title: Memory and loop id completion
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • After /mem show, /mem edit, /mem confirm, /mem forget, /forget, or /done, Tab completes ids from the stores.
  • Memory candidates show a truncated text preview; loop candidates include only open loops.
  • Ids are read at completion time, so a memory added earlier in the session is immediately completable.
  • The logic is split into a pure id_query/id_candidates pair with a unit test.

Acceptance

  • A memory id prefix resolves to the matching entry.
  • The replacement is the bare id; display carries the text preview.
  • Closed loops are excluded from /done completion.
  • Non-id commands still get command completion.

Notes

This is the payoff of short ids: they are easy to type, and now easy to recall without leaving the prompt.

cards.title: Export from the REPL
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • /export writes the current thread as Markdown without leaving the REPL.
  • With no argument it lands at ~/.niuse/export-<thread>.md; an argument is a path, resolved against the session's current /cd directory.
  • The exported file keeps the existing 0600 mode and protocol-block stripping.
  • The default and relative path rules have unit tests.

Acceptance

  • /export /tmp/x.md wrote a private file from a live REPL.
  • The default name derives from the thread file stem.
  • Relative paths follow the runtime cwd, not the process start directory.
  • /help and completion list the command.

Notes

Export is how a session becomes reviewable by a human. It should not require quitting the conversation first.

cards.title: Path completion for cd and export
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Tab after /cd lists directories only; Tab after /export lists files and directories.
  • Relative fragments resolve against the session's current working directory, including after /cd.
  • ~/ fragments resolve against $HOME; bare ~, ., and .. complete to ~/, ./, and ../; absolute fragments against their own root.
  • Directory replacements end with /; hidden entries appear only when the fragment starts with ..

Acceptance

  • Directories and files are filtered and sorted.
  • /cd completion never offers a regular file.
  • The completer shares the live cwd with the REPL, so /cd takes effect immediately.
  • Bare ~, ., and .. complete with a trailing slash.
  • Pure path helpers have unit tests.

Notes

Path completion is the one place where the completer needs mutable state; an Arc<Mutex<PathBuf>> keeps it in sync without making App global.

cards.title: Multi-line input with backslash continuation
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • On a terminal, a line ending with \ keeps the editor open instead of submitting.
  • Continuation lines are joined with a newline and trailing whitespace is trimmed per line.
  • The joined prompt is one history entry and one user message.
  • Piped input is unchanged, so scripts and tests still submit per line.

Acceptance

  • hello \ + there produced a single user_message with hello\nthere.
  • The join helper has a unit test.
  • The continuation hint appears in /help.
  • No extra dependency.

Notes

This is for pasted instructions and multi-paragraph context. It is deliberately a visible backslash, not an invisible mode.

cards.title: Switch models without restarting
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • /model prints the current model and provider.
  • /model <name> rebuilds the provider for the same preset with the new model; the next turn uses it.
  • /model default drops the override and returns to the provider's default model.
  • A failed rebuild reports the error and keeps the previous model.
  • The provider is only rebuilt between turns.

Acceptance

  • /model and /model default print the expected model.
  • default is case-insensitive and covered by a unit test.
  • /help and completion list the command.
  • Switching does not rewrite the system prompt or the thread.

Notes

Rebuilding the provider re-resolves the credential, which is the same path startup uses. No second provider configuration is stored.

cards.title: Session token totals with /cost
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • /cost sums the turn_end usage already recorded in the current thread log.
  • It reports turns, input, output, and cached tokens; compact counts like 3.6k.
  • Resumed threads include their earlier turns, because the log is the source.
  • No in-memory counter is added; the aggregation is a pure function over events.

Acceptance

  • The dogfood thread reported 2 turns · 3.6k in · 149 out.
  • Two synthetic events aggregate correctly in a unit test.
  • /help and completion list the command.
  • No new state or dependency.

Notes

Per-turn usage is for pacing; /cost is for "what has this thread actually spent". Both read the same recorded events.

cards.title: Colored approval diffs
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Approval summaries are bold; warnings are yellow.
  • Diff headers are bold, additions green, removals red, hunk headers cyan.
  • Styling applies only on a TTY and is suppressed by NO_COLOR or a pipe.
  • The style classifier is a pure function with a unit test.

Acceptance

  • +, -, @@, and file headers map to distinct styles.
  • Context lines are unchanged.
  • The prompt and the 80-line cap are untouched.
  • No new dependency.

Notes

Color is the cheapest way to make a long diff scannable before a y/N decision. The decision itself is still one line.

cards.title: Kind counts in the memory header
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem list shows a per-kind breakdown in the header, e.g. 6 条记忆（preference 2 · lesson 4）.
  • An empty store prints no parenthetical.
  • JSON output is unchanged; the summary is text-only.
  • The counting helper has a unit test.

Acceptance

  • Preference and lesson counts come from the loaded entries.
  • Empty stores stay terse.
  • --kind filtering still leaves the global header intact.
  • No storage change.

Notes

The first question about a memory store is usually "is this mostly preferences or lessons". Answering it in the header avoids a second command.

cards.title: Kind counts in status
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse status shows preference and lesson counts next to the memory total.
  • status --json exposes memory.preferences and memory.lessons.
  • The CLI integration test asserts both zero-state fields.
  • mem list and status now describe the store the same way.

Acceptance

  • Text output reads 6 条（preference 3 · lesson 3；…）.
  • JSON parses with the new fields.
  • Empty stores report zeros, not missing keys.
  • No storage or prompt change.

Notes

Two commands answering "what is in memory" should not disagree about the shape of the answer.

cards.title: Memory reviews are measured
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • mem review presents the oldest confirmed entries first and states how many are already expired.
  • Each expired entry is marked individually.
  • Keeping or deleting during review records mem_review_accept or mem_review_delete.
  • stats and stats --json report mem_reviews_kept and mem_reviews_deleted.

Acceptance

  • Expired entries are visible before a decision, not silent.
  • The two metric kinds are covered by the summariser test.
  • JSON includes the new fields.
  • A metric write failure is a warning, not a lost review.

Notes

Review was the one memory path with no evidence trail. A ten-day dogfood cannot argue about pruning if the decisions are invisible.

cards.title: Back up memory before prune
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • mem prune --apply copies both memory files to ~/.niuse/backups/prune-<millis>/ before deleting anything.
  • The backup directory is 0700; copied files are 0600.
  • A failed copy aborts the prune; the store is not modified.
  • The prune test asserts the deleted entry survives in the backup.

Acceptance

  • Backup contains the deleted lesson text.
  • Directory mode is asserted on Unix.
  • Dry run writes no backup.
  • No new dependency.

Notes

Hard delete with no undo is the one memory operation that cannot be reviewed after the fact. A timestamped copy is cheaper than a tombstone format.

cards.title: Readable thread titles
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • The first user message of a thread supplies a one-line title, truncated to 60 characters with an ellipsis.
  • threads prints the title beneath the metrics line; threads --json adds title.
  • The title is derived at read time; no new field is written to the session log.
  • A unit test covers first-message selection and the empty case.

Acceptance

  • The title comes from the first non-empty user message.
  • Later messages do not replace it.
  • JSON carries title as a string or null.
  • No event-log change.

Notes

A list of timestamped files is not a memory of what you were doing. Deriving the title keeps the log untouched and still answers "which one was this".

cards.title: Prune reports freed bytes
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • mem prune --apply reports how many bytes the deletion freed.
  • Byte totals come from the two memory files before and after.
  • The human-readable formatter is shared with the thread listing.
  • memory_bytes has a unit test.

Acceptance

  • Empty stores report zero bytes.
  • Adding one entry makes the total positive.
  • The formatter is reused instead of duplicated.
  • Failure to compute sizes cannot fail the prune.

Notes

Deleting a handful of lines is not about disk pressure; the number is a sanity check that something actually changed. Board priorities only allow P0-P2, so this sits at P2 in practice.

cards.title: Grouped help
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • /help is grouped by purpose: conversation, memory, promises/journal, session, model/cost, identity/settings, debugging.
  • The duplicate /export entry is gone and columns line up.
  • Help lives in one raw string; a test asserts every command appears.
  • No command behavior changes.

Acceptance

  • Every documented command is present in the help text.
  • The continuation hint and review keys are correct.
  • The test fails if a future command is omitted from the list check.
  • Output remains plain text.

Notes

The command count crossed twenty. A flat list stops being scannable before it stops being useful.

cards.title: Doctor checks private files
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • doctor checks ~/.niuse/history (expected 0600) and ~/.niuse/backups/ (expected 0700).
  • Missing paths report not created yet rather than a failure.
  • Group- or world-readable modes produce a warning with the exact chmod hint.
  • The mode predicate has a unit test; no new permission repair is attempted automatically.

Acceptance

  • A 0600 history reports ok.
  • A 0644 history produces a warning naming the expected mode.
  • Absent history/backups are not warnings.
  • is_private_mode is tested across private and leaky modes.

Notes

History contains prompts, which can contain anything. Being unreadable by other local users is part of the privacy story, so it belongs in the same check as the stores.

cards.title: Full diff on demand at approval
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • The approval prompt still shows at most 80 diff lines by default.
  • When the preview was capped, d prints the complete diff and asks again; y accepts, anything else denies.
  • If nothing was capped, d is not offered and is treated as a denial.
  • Parsing of y/yes/d/diff is a pure function with a unit test.

Acceptance

  • d only appears when the preview is truncated.
  • d reprints the full preview without deciding.
  • Denial remains the default for unknown input.
  • The 80-line default cap is unchanged.

Notes

Reviewing a large edit from a terminal should be possible without approving it first. The extra key keeps the common case short.

cards.title: Filter memory by tag
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • mem list --tag rust and mem search <q> --tag rust filter by tag, case-insensitively.
  • --tag composes with --kind, --all, --fresh, and --json.
  • The end-to-end CLI test adds two tagged entries and checks both filters.
  • JSON output keeps the same shape.

Acceptance

  • Listing by tag returns only matching entries.
  • Searching with a non-matching tag returns [].
  • Case-insensitive tag comparison.
  • No storage change.

Notes

Kind answers what a memory is; tags answer which subject it belongs to. Both are cheap filters over an in-memory list.

cards.title: Day zero means the whole journal
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse journal --days 0 lists every entry, matching stats --days 0.
  • Positive windows keep their existing behavior.
  • The window conversion is a pure helper with a unit test.
  • JSON output follows the same rule.

Acceptance

  • 0 maps to the full journal.
  • 7 still means seven days.
  • README documents the convention.
  • No storage change.

Notes

Two commands already accepted 0 as "all time"; the journal was the odd one out. Consistency beats a special case.

cards.title: Edit a memory during review
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • The review prompt gains [e]; it opens $EDITOR with the current text.
  • Saving a changed, non-empty, secret-free text updates it and refreshes the confirmation date.
  • Empty, unchanged, or secret-bearing edits are refused without touching the file.
  • The action records mem_review_edit; stats reports kept/edited/deleted on a dedicated review line.

Acceptance

  • An edit confirms the entry and records a metric.
  • Secret patterns are refused at review time too.
  • A vanished entry is reported, not panicked.
  • Stats text and JSON carry the edited count.

Notes

Review used to force a binary keep/delete choice on stale text. Editing is the third option that does not lose the fact but fixes the wording.

cards.title: Usage is per run, not per step
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Found by a self-dogfood write task: one prompt produced four usage lines and /cost reported four turns.
  • AgentEvent::TurnEnd fires per model step, not per user turn.
  • The renderer now accumulates usage and prints one line per run: 2 steps · 3.9k in · ….
  • /cost counts user_message events as turns and still sums turn_end usage for tokens.

Acceptance

  • A multi-step run prints exactly one usage line.
  • /cost counts user messages, not steps.
  • The aggregation test includes two user messages and two steps.
  • Token totals are unchanged in meaning.

Notes

"Turn" meant two different things in two places. The transcript now shows steps explicitly; /cost answers "how much did this conversation spend".

cards.title: Local dates for the human calendar
cards.body_html:
Problem

Date::today() was UTC. At 01:35 local (UTC+8) on 2026-10-22, a self-check wrote journal and memory entries dated 2026-10-21. For a daily companion, "today" disagreeing with the user's calendar for the first eight hours of the day is surprising.

Decision

  • User-facing dates follow the machine's local calendar. Date::today() uses chrono::Local; journal and memory labels are local dates.
  • Metrics trends group by local day too. Date::from_millis_local maps epoch milliseconds to the local calendar day, so a late-evening turn appears on the day the user experienced it.
  • Event timestamps stay UTC epoch milliseconds. Session logs and metrics.jsonl remain machine-comparable; only the derived day label is local.
  • Storage stays YYYY-MM-DD; no offset is written into the Markdown.

Why local over UTC

The date is a human-facing label: "what did I do today", "when did I last confirm this". UTC is the right choice for ordering events and comparing machines, not for the calendar the user reads. Frameworks that store UTC timestamps usually still render dates in the user's timezone; this is that split, without adding a timezone field per entry.

Consequences

  • Two machines in different timezones can label the same instant differently; that is the intended behavior for daily notes.
  • Tests use explicit dates except Date::today and the millis-mapping test, which compare against chrono::Local.
  • niuse-core gains chrono with the clock feature; MSRV stays 1.88.
  • Metrics day keys are local; the underlying timestamps are unchanged.

Acceptance

  • A memory added at 09:24 local on 2026-10-22 is dated 2026-10-22.
  • Date::today matches chrono::Local's date.
  • Date::from_millis_local matches the local calendar day.
  • stats --trend groups metrics by local day.
  • README no longer claims UTC dates.

cards.title: Bootstrap progress only on a TTY
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • The \r[1/2] 抽取中… progress line is written only when stderr is a terminal.
  • Non-TTY runs no longer put carriage returns into captured logs; the summary still prints.
  • Per-session failures still skip that session and continue.
  • No behavior change for interactive use.

Acceptance

  • Piped bootstrap output contains no carriage returns.
  • Interactive runs still show in-place progress.
  • Skipped sessions keep their warning.
  • The final eprintln! is gated with the same flag.

Notes

Found while running bootstrap from a captured shell: the progress line is fine on a terminal and noise in a log. The summary is the durable output.

cards.title: Bootstrap fails when every session fails
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Per-session extraction errors are still skipped, so one bad transcript does not kill the run.
  • If every selected session failed and none was extracted, bootstrap exits non-zero with an explicit message.
  • The existing inbox is left untouched on that path; no empty rewrite pretends success.
  • A partial failure still writes whatever succeeded.

Acceptance

  • An all-failed run exits 1 with all N session(s) failed.
  • The inbox file is byte-identical after the failure.
  • The per-session skip … warning remains.
  • The success path and --profile-only are unchanged.

Notes

Found when the provider was unreachable: the old behavior printed 0 new candidate(s) and exited 0, which reads as "nothing to remember" rather than "the extraction never ran".

cards.title: Relative --thread paths resolve consistently
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • --thread is treated as a path argument: relative paths resolve against the process working directory, absolute paths are kept.
  • The same helper feeds App, threads, and status, so the active marker and status agree.
  • With no --thread, the store's session path is used exactly as before.
  • The absolute/default cases have a unit test.

Acceptance

  • A relative thread path can no longer miss the active marker because one copy stayed relative.
  • --thread with an absolute path is unchanged.
  • The default path is unchanged.
  • One resolution point instead of three inline copies.
  • End-to-end: from the home directory, --thread thread.jsonl reports active: true.

Notes

Three call sites each did unwrap_or_else(session_path); the path was never normalized. The bug only showed when a relative path met the absolute listing.

cards.title: List one-shot exec sessions
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse exec writes its log under ~/.niuse/sessions/; those logs were invisible in threads.
  • New niuse sessions [--json] lists them with age, events, bytes, path, and a derived title.
  • threads keeps its meaning: the active thread plus archived chapters, with the active marker.
  • The directory scan is shared by both listings.

Acceptance

  • A one-shot log appears with its first user message as title.
  • active is false for every one-shot.
  • JSON parses; text output is readable.
  • threads output is unchanged.

Notes

exec was creating durable files with no discovery path. A separate command keeps "thread" semantics intact while making the logs findable.

cards.title: Corrupt session lines are tolerated
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • A session log with a bad JSON line loads its valid events; the loader warns on stderr.
  • sessions --json still lists it, with the valid event count and a title from the first readable user message.
  • export --session succeeds on the same file and writes a 0600 Markdown file.
  • An end-to-end CLI test pins both behaviors.

Acceptance

  • events counts only decodable lines.
  • The title comes from the readable user message.
  • Export exits zero and contains that message.
  • No new dependency.

Notes

Session logs are append-only files that can be truncated by a crash or edited by hand. Listing and export should degrade to the readable prefix, not refuse the whole file.

cards.title: Export uses a readable title
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Exported Markdown starts with the first user message (one line, 60 chars) instead of the fixed # niuse thread.
  • The existing title derivation is reused, so threads, threads --json, and export agree.
  • Empty or unreadable logs fall back to niuse thread.
  • The metadata blockquote and body are unchanged.

Acceptance

  • An exec log exports as # 只回答两个字：pong.
  • The fallback keeps old exports readable.
  • Protocol blocks and 0600 behavior are untouched.
  • No new state or dependency.

Notes

An exported file is often the only artifact a human sees. Its first line should say what the session was about.

cards.title: Declare the real MSRV: 1.88
cards.body_html:
Problem

The workspace declared rust-version = "1.85", but cargo +1.85.0 check failed: several transitive dependencies require 1.88. Worse, rustyline 19 uses the cfg_select! macro, which is still unstable on 1.92, so the interactive REPL had silently raised the effective MSRV beyond the declared one.

Fix

  • Pin rustyline = "15": the API used here (Editor, FileHistory, Completer, Validator, history) is unchanged, and it builds on stable 1.88.
  • Set rust-version = "1.88" and README to match.
  • Verified with cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace --all-targets.

Acceptance

  • cargo +1.88.0 check passes for the whole workspace.
  • The full workspace test suite passes under 1.88 (verified 2026-10-22).
  • The stable toolchain still passes the full check script.
  • README and Cargo agree.
  • Interactive editing behavior is unchanged.

Notes

A false MSRV is worse than a higher one: contributors on the declared version get a wall of dependency errors. The dependency tree, not our own syntax, sets the floor.

cards.title: Oversized promise does not hide the rest
cards.body_html:
Problem

The loop section stopped at the first promise that did not fit the 300-token budget. A single long, overdue promise could therefore hide every shorter promise behind it.

Fix

  • Skip an oversized line and keep scanning; the budget is unchanged.
  • A unit test puts a 2,000-character overdue promise before a short one and asserts the short one is injected.

Acceptance

  • The short promise appears in the prompt.
  • The oversized one does not.
  • The budget and ordering are unchanged.
  • No storage or protocol change.

Notes

Memory lines already used continue; loops used break. The asymmetry was accidental, not a policy.

cards.title: Oversized journal day does not hide older ones
cards.body_html:
Problem

The journal section stopped at the first day that did not fit the 600-token budget. One long day (a big debugging session) could hide every earlier day from the prompt.

Fix

  • Skip the oversized day and keep scanning, matching the memory and loop sections.
  • A unit test puts a 4,000-character day before a short one and asserts the short one is injected.

Acceptance

  • The older small day reaches the prompt.
  • The oversized day is omitted.
  • Budget and chronological ordering are unchanged.
  • No storage change.

Notes

Recency is the ordering, not a reason to drop everything after one bad day. All three budgeted sections now use the same skip rule.

cards.title: Doctor flags malformed memory sections
cards.body_html:
Problem

Memory files are hand-editable Markdown. A typo in the required fields makes a ### m-… section silently unparseable: the entry disappears from prompts and listings with no signal.

Fix

  • Store::memory_issues() compares ### m-… headers with parsed entries per file.
  • doctor reports all memory sections parsed, a warning naming the file and the unparsed section count, a warning when a file has content but no parseable entries, or stray non-field lines among valid entries.
  • No automatic repair; the file stays the user's.

Acceptance

  • A store with one valid and one broken section reports one issue.
  • A file containing only garbage reports has content but no parseable entries.
  • Stray prose among valid entries is reported.
  • A clean store reports none.
  • The doctor warning names preferences.md.
  • The check is read-only.

Notes

Silent data loss is worse than a noisy warning here: the whole point of Markdown storage is that a human can edit it.

cards.title: Doctor checks loops and journal too
cards.body_html:
Problem

The memory parse check stopped at memory. loops.md and journal/*.md are hand-editable too; a malformed promise line or an invalid date heading silently disappears from prompts and listings.

Fix

  • Store::content_issues() extends memory_issues() with:
    • loops: - [ lines versus parsed promises, plus stray non-comment lines;
    • journal: ## headings and - bullets versus parsed days/bullets per file, plus stray non-comment lines.
  • doctor reports one parse check for all three stores.
  • The unit test plants a malformed loop and an invalid journal heading and asserts both are named.
  • No automatic repair; files stay human-owned.

Acceptance

  • A malformed promise line is reported as loops.md.
  • An invalid date heading, its bullet, and a stray prose line are reported for the journal file.
  • Clean stores report all stored content parsed.
  • The check is read-only.

Notes

Same principle as M2-064: Markdown is editable, so malformed content must be visible, not silently dropped.

cards.title: Token usage in stats
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • The renderer exposes accumulated usage for the run.
  • REPL and exec append a tokens metric with input,output,cached after a run that used tokens.
  • stats sums those values and prints tokens 2k in · 400 out · 1.2k cached; JSON exposes the three totals.
  • Malformed token details are ignored, like other malformed metrics.

Acceptance

  • Two synthetic records sum to 2000 / 400 / 1200.
  • Text uses compact counts; JSON uses raw numbers.
  • A run with zero usage writes no metric.
  • The summariser test covers the new kind.
  • A real exec wrote 1660,61,1408 and stats --json summed it.

Notes

/cost answers "this thread"; stats now answers "this week". Both read recorded facts, not an in-memory counter.

cards.title: Bootstrap review supports edit
cards.body_html:
Problem

The plan's cold-start section says niuse review supports y accept, n discard, and e edit. The implementation only had y, n, s, and q; an almost-right candidate had to be accepted or discarded, not fixed.

Fix

  • Add [e] 编辑: open $EDITOR, refuse empty or unchanged results, scan for secrets, then accept the edited text.
  • The accepted entry keeps the source session id; review_accept is recorded.
  • Prompt, plan, and behavior now agree.

Acceptance

  • e with a scripted editor changed the candidate text before accepting.
  • The edited entry kept the style tag and s1 source.
  • Empty/secret edits are refused without writing.
  • n still discards and records review_discard.

Notes

This was found by comparing the plan with the implementation, not by a failing test. The plan is the spec for the cold-start ritual.

cards.title: Rejected tags are suppressed for the session
cards.body_html:
Problem

The plan promises that after a memory rejection, the same tags are not proposed again in that session. The implementation discarded the candidate but kept offering the same tag, which is the confirmation fatigue the plan is trying to avoid.

Fix

  • App keeps a session-local set of rejected tags.
  • Discarding a candidate (plain or conflict path) records its tags.
  • A later candidate carrying any rejected tag is skipped and counted under suppress.
  • The tag predicate is a pure function with a unit test.

Acceptance

  • Case-insensitive tag matching.
  • Untagged candidates are not suppressed by tags.
  • Rejection from both the normal and conflict prompts records tags.
  • s still stops all proposals for the session.

Notes

The set lives only in memory; a new session starts clean. This is a fatigue valve, not a permanent mute.

cards.title: Daily token trend
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Per-day summaries now accumulate input/output/cached tokens.
  • stats --trend prints 12k in · 400 out beside turns and acceptance, plus · N cached when the day had cache hits.
  • stats --json day records carry the three token fields.
  • Token detail parsing is one helper shared by the total and daily paths.

Acceptance

  • A day with a token record reports its counts.
  • The trend line includes compact input/output numbers and cached when non-zero.
  • JSON day entries gain the fields without breaking existing keys.
  • The daily-summary test covers tokens.

Notes

Totals answer "what did this week cost"; the trend answers "is it getting cheaper or noisier".

cards.title: List threads and sessions inside the REPL
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • /threads prints the active thread and archived chapters without leaving the session.
  • /sessions prints one-shot exec logs.
  • Both reuse the CLI commands, so paths, titles, and age columns stay identical.
  • /help groups them under the session section; completion lists both.

Acceptance

  • The commands are part of the slash list and help coverage test.
  • Output is the same as niuse threads / niuse sessions.
  • No new state.
  • Piped sessions cannot reach them; this is TTY/REPL convenience.

Notes

Leaving the conversation to inspect where you are is unnecessary ceremony. The commands read the same files the CLI reads.

cards.title: Resume a thread by index
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • threads numbers its rows; the active thread is still marked with *.
  • /resume <n> closes the current log, opens the n-th entry, and reloads history.
  • The index is one-based and matches the listing order at read time.
  • Resuming the current thread is a no-op with a message.
  • thread_at has a unit test for 0, 1, 2, and out-of-range.

Acceptance

  • threads shows [1], [2], …
  • /resume 1 resolves the same path the listing shows.
  • The old log gets a session_end before switching.
  • Invalid or missing indexes do not leave the session.
  • End-to-end: /new → /threads shows [1] [2] → /resume 2 → /cost reports the archived thread's 2 turns.

Notes

Numbers are computed per command, not stored; new archives can shift them, so the listing and the resume normally happen together.

cards.title: New after resume starts a fresh log
cards.body_html:
Problem

After resuming an archive, /new archived the resumed thread but reopened the existing thread.jsonl instead of creating a fresh one, so the "new" line silently reused the old session start.

Two archives created within the same millisecond also shared a destination name, and rename would replace the earlier file.

Fix

  • /new archives the stale active log when the current thread is not thread.jsonl, then opens a genuinely fresh one.
  • Archive names gain a -1, -2 suffix until the path is free.
  • unique_archive_path has a same-stamp unit test.
  • End-to-end: /new → /resume 2 → /new left two archives (thread-…812 and thread-…812-1) and a fresh active log.

Acceptance

  • The stale active log is archived, not reused.
  • Same-millisecond archives get distinct names.
  • The active log has exactly one new session_start.
  • The /threads listing shows active, original, and stale as separate rows.

Notes

Both bugs only appear in the resume path; normal /new from the active thread already archived first.

cards.title: Failed review actions keep the candidate
cards.body_html:
Problem

In niuse review, the e path advanced past the candidate when the editor was abandoned, produced empty text, or triggered the secret scan. The y path did the same when the unedited candidate itself tripped the scan. The candidate vanished from both the inbox and memory — neither accepted nor explicitly discarded.

Fix

  • Every failed edit, and a y refused by the secret scan, now prints 保留到下次 and pushes the candidate back onto remaining.
  • Accepting an edited candidate still removes it from the inbox and records review_accept.
  • Manual check with a secret-bearing candidate: y refused, inbox still contains the entry, summary says 剩余 1 条, no memory file is written.

Acceptance

  • Abandoned edit keeps the candidate.
  • Empty edit keeps the candidate.
  • Secret-bearing edit keeps the candidate.
  • A y refused for a secret keeps the candidate pending.
  • A successful edit still accepts and clears it.

Notes

The only actions that should destroy a candidate are an explicit accept or discard. An editor failure is not a decision.

cards.title: Unknown config keys are rejected
cards.body_html:
Problem

config.toml was parsed without deny_unknown_fields, so provder = "deepseek" was silently ignored and the built-in default was used. The user sees the typo in the file and a different behavior at runtime.

Fix

  • FileConfig and Defaults deny unknown fields.
  • config effective, doctor, and any provider-building command now fail with the TOML parse error instead of guessing.
  • The settings test covers a misspelled field and an unknown top-level key.

Acceptance

  • provder under [defaults] is a parse error.
  • An unknown top-level key is a parse error.
  • Empty and valid files still parse.
  • No runtime fallback hides the typo.

Notes

A config file is a contract with the user; silently ignoring a line is the opposite of reviewable.

cards.title: Memory id completion accepts the m- prefix
cards.body_html:
Problem

Listings show memory ids as m-7f3a, but Tab completion matched only the bare 7f3a. Typing the visible form /mem show m-7f and pressing Tab produced no candidates.

Fix

  • The memory completer strips an optional m- before matching and puts it back in both display and replacement.
  • Loop ids already contained l-; that path is unchanged.
  • The id-completion test now covers both bare and prefixed fragments.

Acceptance

  • /mem show m-<prefix> completes to m-<id>.
  • Bare prefixes still complete to the bare id.
  • Loop completion remains l-<id>.
  • Display and replacement agree.

Notes

Completion should accept the spelling the product prints. This was a small mismatch between two surfaces of the same id.

cards.title: Status shows whether a user profile exists
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse status prints a user line next to identity, with 已设置 / 未设置.
  • status --json already carried the boolean; this aligns the text view.
  • The CLI integration test asserts the line exists.

Acceptance

  • The text view reports profile presence.
  • JSON is unchanged.
  • Empty and populated homes both work.
  • No prompt or storage change.

Notes

Identity and user are the two human-authored layers; showing only one of them made the status page look like the profile did not exist.

cards.title: Tilde paths expand in cd and export
cards.body_html:
Problem

Path completion resolved ~/ against $HOME, so Tab suggested it, but /cd ~/project joined the literal ~ to the current directory and failed. /export ~/out.md did the same.

Fix

  • One expand_tilde helper handles ~ and ~/… using $HOME; unrelated paths pass through.
  • /cd and /export both use it before relative-path joining.
  • Unit test covers ~/out.md, bare ~, and a plain relative path.
  • Manual check: /cd ~ reports cwd: /home/<user>.

Acceptance

  • Bare ~ becomes $HOME.
  • ~/… becomes $HOME/….
  • Plain paths are unchanged.
  • Completion and execution now agree.

Notes

This was a mismatch between what completion advertised and what the command did. $HOME missing falls back to a literal path rather than panicking.

cards.title: Status reports the version
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse status begins with version 0.1.0.
  • status --json carries the same string as version.
  • The CLI test asserts a non-empty version field.
  • The value comes from CARGO_PKG_VERSION; no second constant.

Acceptance

  • Text and JSON report the package version.
  • The value is not hardcoded in the test.
  • No prompt or storage change.
  • Works on an empty home.

Notes

Bug reports need the binary version and the pinned niucode revision; doctor already shows the pin.

cards.title: Editor temp files are private
cards.body_html:
Problem

$EDITOR helpers wrote identity, user, memory, and candidate text to /tmp/niuse-edit-<pid>.md with default permissions — typically 0644, readable by other local users, and containing secrets before the post-edit scan runs.

Fix

  • The temp file is opened with create_new and mode 0600 on Unix, so it is private from creation, not after a chmod race.
  • The name includes the pid and nanosecond stamp; concurrent edits cannot share a path.
  • Cleanup still removes the file after the editor exits; a failed write removes it too.
  • A unit test checks content, uniqueness, and 0600.

Acceptance

  • Mode is 0600 at creation.
  • Two calls produce distinct paths.
  • The original text is written intact.
  • The file is removed on the normal path.

Notes

The secret scan protects the store; it does not protect a world-readable scratch file that existed before the scan.

cards.title: Atomic store writes create private temp files
cards.body_html:
Problem

Every store write used path.with_extension("tmp"): a predictable name, created with default 0644, then chmodded to 0600 and renamed. The file was briefly world-readable, and a local attacker could pre-create that path as a symlink to a victim file.

Fix

  • The temp name is .<file>.tmp-<pid>-<nanos>, created with create_new and mode 0600 on Unix.
  • The final rename preserves those permissions; no chmod window.
  • A failed write or rename removes the temp file.
  • A Unix test pre-creates the old predictable path as a symlink and verifies the victim is untouched.

Acceptance

  • Temp mode is 0600 at creation.
  • The predictable identity.tmp symlink is not followed.
  • The destination still receives the new content.
  • No leftover temp file on the success path.

Notes

Atomicity and privacy are different properties; the old code had the first and only eventually the second.

cards.title: Export files are private at creation
cards.body_html:
Problem

write_export used fs::write and chmodded to 0600 afterwards. A new export in a shared directory was readable for a short window, and exports can contain anything the session contained.

Fix

  • The file is opened with create/truncate and mode 0600 on Unix, so a new file is private from the first byte.
  • The post-write chmod stays as a repair for pre-existing world-readable files.
  • Existing export tests still assert 0600 on the result.

Acceptance

  • New exports are created 0600.
  • Existing files are still repaired to 0600.
  • Content and truncation behavior are unchanged.
  • No new dependency.

Notes

The same pattern as the store and editor fixes: create private, do not create then repair.

cards.title: Editor command respects arguments and VISUAL
cards.body_html:
Problem

$EDITOR was passed whole to Command::new, so a common value like code --wait was treated as one executable name and failed. An empty $EDITOR failed the same way, and $VISUAL was ignored.

Fix

  • $VISUAL wins, then $EDITOR, then vi.
  • The value is split into program plus arguments; the temp path is appended as the final argument.
  • Empty values fall back to vi.
  • A pure editor_parts test covers code --wait, empty, and a bare program.

Acceptance

  • code --wait becomes program plus one argument.
  • Empty input yields vi.
  • The edited file path is still the last argument.
  • Temporary files stay private.

Notes

This does not attempt shell quoting; editors with quoted paths should be wrapped in a small script. Ordinary flags are the common case.

cards.title: Thread logs are private from creation
cards.body_html:
Problem

open_thread used File::create and then set_private. A new thread in a user-supplied --thread path was briefly 0644, and an existing thread with loose permissions was never repaired on open.

Fix

  • New thread files are opened with create_new and mode 0600 on Unix.
  • set_private now runs on every open, repairing an existing loose file.
  • Unix tests cover creation mode and repair of a manually chmodded 0644 file.

Acceptance

  • A new thread file is 0600 immediately.
  • An existing 0644 thread becomes 0600 on open.
  • Content and session start behavior are unchanged.
  • No new dependency.

Notes

Session logs contain prompts and tool output; the file should never be world-readable, even for a moment.

cards.title: Metrics file is private at creation
cards.body_html:
Problem

append_metric opened metrics.jsonl without a creation mode and chmodded to 0600 afterwards. It was the last writer using the create-then-repair pattern.

Fix

  • The open options set mode 0600 on Unix; the existing chmod remains as a repair for old files.
  • The existing metrics test continues to assert the final mode and content order.

Acceptance

  • New metric files are 0600 at creation.
  • Existing loose files are repaired.
  • Append order and sanitization are unchanged.
  • All store writers now use create-private-then-write.

Notes

With store, editor, export, thread, and metrics fixed, no production writer creates a readable file before setting permissions.

cards.title: Shell completions
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse completions <shell> prints a completion script for bash, zsh, fish, powershell, or elvish.
  • The command returns before store discovery/init, so it works without a home and creates nothing.
  • The CLI test asserts output content and that the home path is untouched.
  • README lists the command.

Acceptance

  • completions bash prints a _niuse function.
  • No ~/.niuse is created.
  • clap_complete is the only new dependency.
  • Other commands are unchanged.

Notes

Completions for the slash commands are provided by rustyline inside the REPL; this covers the outer CLI.

cards.title: Slash-command errors do not end the session
cards.body_html:
Problem

The run loop used self.command(...)?. A typo such as /mem show nope, an invalid /cd, or a failed /export propagated out of the loop, printed Error: and exited the whole REPL.

Fix

  • Command errors are printed in place and the loop continues.
  • Ok(Flow::Quit) still exits; Ok(Flow::Continue) continues.
  • Manual check: /mem show nope printed the error, /status still ran, /quit exited zero.

Acceptance

  • A failed command prints an error and keeps the prompt.
  • The next command still executes.
  • /quit returns zero.
  • Turn errors are unchanged.

Notes

Interactive tools should treat a bad command like a shell does: report and keep the prompt. Only explicit quit or a broken terminal should end the session.

cards.title: Show only overdue promises
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse loops list --overdue keeps only open promises whose due date is before today.
  • JSON carries the same filter; the header says N 条逾期 instead of the unfiltered totals.
  • Works with --all for consistency; done promises are never overdue.
  • End-to-end test adds one late and one future promise and asserts only the late one appears.

Acceptance

  • Only overdue loops are listed.
  • JSON overdue is true for the result.
  • The header does not claim three open promises when none are shown.
  • No filter keeps the old output.

Notes

The daily question is "what is late", not "what exists". The unfiltered list remains the default.

cards.title: Effective config as JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse config effective --json emits provider, model, sandbox, approval, network, and max_steps.
  • A missing model is null, matching the runtime's provider-default meaning.
  • The text view is unchanged when the flag is absent.
  • An end-to-end CLI test parses the object and checks defaults.

Acceptance

  • JSON parses and carries the six settings.
  • model is null when unset.
  • max_steps stays numeric.
  • No provider or credential is constructed.

Notes

config effective now matches the machine-readable style of the rest of the CLI.

cards.title: Single memory as JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse mem show <id> --json emits the same entry shape as mem list --json.
  • The text view is unchanged.
  • An end-to-end test adds an entry, reads its id from the list, and shows it back as JSON.

Acceptance

  • JSON parses with id, text, and tags.
  • The shape matches the list output.
  • The text view is unchanged.
  • No storage change.

Notes

Memory is now machine-readable at both the collection and single-entry level.

cards.title: Profile files as JSON
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • niuse user show --json and niuse identity show --json emit {path, text}.
  • A missing file is text: null, not an empty string; the path is always present.
  • Text output is unchanged.
  • An end-to-end test checks both commands on an empty home.

Acceptance

  • Both objects parse and carry an absolute path.
  • Missing text is null.
  • Text views are unchanged.
  • No storage change.

Notes

The two human-authored layers now have the same machine-readable shape as memory and journal.

cards.title: One-command dogfood row
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • scripts/dogfood.sh "note" reads niuse stats --days 1 --json and inserts today's row into docs/dogfood.md.
  • The date comes from the local calendar, matching journal and memory.
  • Running it twice in one day replaces the row instead of duplicating it; the YYYY-MM-DD placeholder is removed.
  • --file supports a scratch copy; NIUSE_BIN / NIUSE_HOME select the binary and store.
  • The guide explains that this records real use, not a reconstruction.

Acceptance

  • First run inserts one row and removes the placeholder.
  • Second run replaces the same-day row; the count stays one.
  • Notes are pipe-escaped.
  • An end-to-end shell test in scripts/check.sh covers one row, replacement, and no duplicate.
  • The script fails clearly when niuse is missing or the table is not found.

Notes

The command only formats numbers that already exist; it cannot make a day count. The ten real days are still the gate.

cards.title: Stats windows follow local calendar days
cards.body_html:
Problem

After day labels moved to the local calendar, stats --days 1 still used a rolling now - 24h cutoff. At 09:00 local it could show yesterday evening plus today, while claiming a one-day window; the labels and the window disagreed.

Fix

  • Date::start_millis_local returns local midnight for a calendar date, using the earliest valid instant across DST transitions.
  • window_start(days) is 0 for all time, otherwise local midnight days - 1 days ago.
  • stats and stats --trend share that cutoff.
  • Tests cover the local-midnight round trip and the one-day/two-day window starts; the CLI help says "local calendar days".

Acceptance

  • --days 1 starts at local midnight today.
  • --days 2 starts at local midnight yesterday.
  • --days 0 still means all time.
  • A DST transition cannot silently shift the cutoff by a day.
  • If a zone skips local midnight, the first valid hour is used instead of zero.

Notes

A day label and a day window should agree; otherwise the trend looks like it has data from a day it filtered out.

cards.title: identity.md is the only name source
cards.body_html:
问题

用户问「你是谁」，真实 REPL 答「我是 niuse」，被纠正后才改口。根因是 persona 的 BASE 硬编码了「你是 niuse」，而 identity.md 只是后面的一节；模型把产品名当成了自己的名字。

修复

  • BASE 不再自称名字，只描述工作方式，并明确「名字、语气与边界由后面的『你是谁』一节定义；产品名不是你的名字」。
  • identity 节增加「唯一真源」优先级：与本 prompt 其他段落（包括产品名）冲突时，以 identity 为准。
  • 协议段把「niuse 会解析」改成「运行时会解析」，减少产品名被当作人格线索。
  • 新增测试 identity_is_the_only_name_source：断言 BASE 不含硬编码名字，identity 的 niubot 与优先级文本都出现。

验收

  • BASE 不再包含「你是 niuse」。
  • identity 节声明唯一真源。
  • 真实模型在 identity 写 niubot 时直接答「我是 niubot」，无需纠正。
  • 现有 prompt 顺序与预算测试不变。

备注

产品名仍然出现在启动 banner、命令和文档里；它只是项目名，不是人格。identity 缺失时 persona 也不自报一个假名字。

cards.title: Release and dependency strategy
cards.body_html:
Scope

  • Decide the niucode dependency: publish niucode crates first, convert to pinned git revisions, or keep the two-checkout build.
  • Add license, repository, description, and other release metadata.
  • Make cargo package / cargo publish --dry-run reproducible.
  • Confirm crate-name availability; rename the crate if needed while keeping the niuse binary.

Acceptance

  • cargo package -p niuse passes (currently blocked by path dependencies).
  • The install path is reproducible on a clean machine.
  • License and naming strategy are documented in the README.

Notes

Findings and options are recorded in distribution.

Current failure: all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging, pointing at the niucode-agent path dependency.

cards.title: Distribution claims match the repository
cards.body_html:
Problem

docs/distribution.md claimed cargo install --git https://github.com/niuverse/niuse worked. A clean clone has no sibling niucode, and the path = "../niuverse/niucode/..." dependencies cannot be fetched, so the command fails before building.

Evidence

  • Cloned the repository into /tmp and ran cargo metadata: failed to load manifest for dependency niucode-agent.
